commitResults.messageTitle: Add pick command to choose a random game
commitResults.messageBody:
Hosts can list the games that fit their group, but the group still
has to agree on one, which wastes time at the start of a game night.

Let's add PickCommand, used as "pick COUNT", which picks one random
game from those that fit COUNT players, or says none fit.

The Random is passed in through a package-private constructor so
tests can control which game is picked.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add rate command to rate games after playing
commitResults.messageBody:
Hosts want pick to favour games the group actually enjoyed (#57).

rate INDEX up|down adds a thumbs up or down, shown in list as +UP/-DOWN
and saved as the named field ratings=UP/DOWN. pick now weights each
game by (up + 1) / (down + 1), so unrated games behave as before and a
disliked game is less likely but never ruled out. edit keeps ratings.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add list command to show all games
commitResults.messageBody:
Users can add games but have no way to see what is in their
collection, so they cannot check what they own or find the number
of a game for later commands such as delete.

Let's add a ListCommand that shows every game numbered from 1, or a
short message when the collection is empty.

Like help and exit, list rejects extra arguments, so a typo such as
"list 5" is reported instead of being silently accepted.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add delete command to remove a game
commitResults.messageBody:
Users cannot remove a game once it is added, so the collection goes
out of date when a game is sold, lost or given away.

Let's add a DeleteCommand that removes the game with the given number
from list, saves the collection, and shows the removed game.

Whether the number exists is checked when the command runs, since
only then is the size of the collection known. A number too large to
fit in an int is reported as not existing, not as "not a whole
number", so the error matches what the user actually did wrong.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add find command to search games by title
commitResults.messageBody:

to locate one game, then read off its number before deleting or
editing it.

Let's add 'find KEYWORD', which shows every game whose title contains
the keyword, ignoring case, together with its number from 'list'.

FindCommand walks the list by position instead of filtering it first,
so each match keeps its original number and can be passed straight to
delete, edit or tag.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add history and unplayed commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Games record their play sessions through log, but the user can only see
when a game was last played, not its full history, and cannot easily find
games that were never played.

Let's add history INDEX, which lists a game's sessions oldest first with a
play count summary, and unplayed, which lists the games with no sessions.

Both commands only read the sessions that log already stores, so the data
file is unchanged. unplayed keeps each game's number from list, as find
does, so the number can be passed straight to log or history.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make find and sort work with extra spaces and any locale

"find ticket  to" finds nothing. find and sort also lower-case text
with the computer's default locale, so on a Turkish system "TITLE"
becomes "tıtle" and no longer matches.

Let's collapse runs of spaces in the find keyword and lower-case with
Locale.ROOT in FindCommand and SortOrder. find now logs its match
count at FINE, like the other commands.

SortOrder.TIME also switches to comparingInt, as suggested on #37,
and a test variable is renamed from sorted to sortedGames.

Let's move finding the games into findUnplayedNumbers and building the
message into formatUnplayed, so execute only decides what to show.
delete now logs at FINE, as other commands that change data do.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add filter command to find games by player count
commitResults.messageBody:
Hosts have to scan the whole collection to work out which games
suit tonight's group.

Add FilterCommand, used as "filter COUNT", which shows only the
games whose player range includes the given count.

Let Parser.parsePlayerCount() take the command's usage string, so
the "is missing" error shows the format of the command being parsed
instead of always showing the add format.

Results are not numbered, because delete uses positions from the
full list and numbering a filtered view would be misleading.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let games record an optional play time and save it
commitResults.messageBody:
Hosts want to pick games that fit the time they have tonight (#22), so a
game needs to know how long it takes. The time is optional because users
may not know it for every game.

The data file stores it as an optional 4th field (TITLE | MIN | MAX | TIME).
Old files without it still load, and an empty field also means no time,
so tags (#23) can be added as a 5th field later.

commitResults.messageTitle: Support /time in add and filter
commitResults.messageBody:
add accepts an optional /time MINUTES, and filter COUNT /time MINUTES
shows only games that take that long or less. Games with no play time
are left out, and filter says how many, so users know why a game they
expected is missing.

Prefixes are now matched only as separate words and may come in any
order, so a title such as Foo/minimal is no longer split. A repeated
prefix is rejected instead of producing a confusing error.

Let games record who they are lent to and save it
commitResults.messageBody:
A game that is lent to a friend cannot be played on game night, so
Game now keeps an optional borrower name. Borrower holds the naming
rules so the parser and the data file accept exactly the same names.

The borrower is saved as an optional sixth field. Earlier fields are
left blank so each field keeps its position, and unset fields are
dropped from the end, so games that are not lent are saved exactly as
before and old data files still load.

GameList#filterByPlayers now skips lent games, so every suggestion
uses one definition of "available". EditCommand copies the borrower
to the edited game, as it already does for tags.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add lend, return and lent commands
commitResults.messageBody:
lend INDEX /to NAME records who borrowed a game, return INDEX puts it
back on the shelf, and lent lists every lent game with its number from
list, so it can be used with return straight away.

Lending a game that is already lent, or returning one that is not, is
reported instead of silently overwriting the borrower, as it is most
likely a wrong INDEX.

commitResults.messageTitle: Leave lent games out of filter and pick, and say why
commitResults.messageBody:
Suggestions should only include games the host can play tonight.
filter, filter /tag and pick leave out lent games and add a note
naming them and their borrowers, so users know why a game they
expected is missing. A lent game is only mentioned if it would
otherwise have matched.

Unavailable games (#53) need one definition of "available", so add

game for a group size.

Move describeLeftOut from LentCommand to GameList, so filter and pick
do not depend on another command. filter /tag matches by tag, so it
passes its own list of lent games.

Rename lent to lentout (ListLentCommand), as lend and lent are easy to
mix up, and give each command its own test class. Also fix two
malformed @@author tags.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let games record a difficulty level and save it
commitResults.messageBody:
Hosts need to avoid games too complicated for new players (#55), so a
game can now record whether it is easy, medium or hard. The level is
optional, and is saved as the named field difficulty=LEVEL, so existing
data files load and save unchanged.

GameList gains one method that applies the player, time and level
conditions together. The notes that explain missing games now take the
level into account, so users are only told about games that could have
matched.

commitResults.messageTitle: Support /diff in add, edit, filter and pick
commitResults.messageBody:
add and edit accept /diff easy|medium|hard, and edit also accepts
/diff none to remove the level. filter, filter /tag and pick accept
/diff to consider only games at that level. Games with no level are
left out and counted in a note, matching how /time treats games with
no play time.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make prefixes case-insensitive, like command words
commitResults.messageBody:
Command words are not case-sensitive, but prefixes were, so
add Y /min 2 /max 3 /TIME 30 failed with a confusing MAX error.
splitByPrefixes now matches prefixes in any case and stores them in
lower case, and quotes each prefix so it is always matched literally.
Also update the Storage Javadoc to describe the full data file format.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove repeated test setup and shorten FilterCommand.execute
commitResults.messageBody:
Several command tests pasted the same game collections, so they now
share SampleGames, which builds a new collection for each test.
FilterCommand.execute was 42 lines; building the criteria, the list
of matches and the notes now happens in separate methods. The output
is unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save the game list to the data file and create it if missing
commitResults.messageBody: Storage.save() writes one game per line (TITLE | MIN | MAX) using Game.toFileString(), so the format stays in one place. It creates the data folder if needed. On startup, GameVault creates an empty data file if it does not exist. GameList.getGames() returns a read-only view so Storage can read the games. Fixes #11

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe the Storage component in the developer guide
commitResults.messageBody: Adds a Storage section covering how games are loaded at startup and saved after each change, and the design alternatives considered (file format, handling invalid lines, how to save). Updated for the optional play time field, and fixes the outdated file format in the data file loading section. Diagram images will be added in a follow-up commit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Support tagging games and filtering by tag
commitResults.messageBody: Adds tag INDEX TAG, untag INDEX TAG and filter /tag TAG so hosts can group games by mood (e.g. party, co-op) and pick suitable ones. Tags are one word, case-insensitive and unique per game. They are saved as an optional fifth TAGS field, so older data files still load. Tag rules live in one Tag class so the parser and data file decoder check tags the same way. edit now keeps a game's tags. Updates help, the UG and tests. Fixes #23

commitResults.messageTitle: Extend tagging with tags list, tags on add, combined filter and multiple tags
commitResults.messageBody: Adds a tags command listing each tag with its game count, so hosts reuse existing tags. add accepts /tag with one or more tags. filter /tag can now be combined with COUNT and /time, e.g. party games for 6 players in 45 minutes. tag and untag accept several tags at once, skipping and reporting tags already present or missing. Updates help, the UG and tests. Builds on #32.

commitResults.messageTitle: Leave unavailable games out of filter and pick
commitResults.messageBody: Game#isAvailable() now also checks isMarkedUnavailable(), so filter, filter /tag and pick skip games marked missing or damaged through the shared check from #50. Following review on #61: unavailable games now show as (unavailable: REASON) to match (lent to NAME), and UnavailableReason.keywords() is the single list used by the usage line and error messages. Also removes an empty games.txt that was committed by mistake in the merge, and updates the UG and DG (including the pick section) to say unavailable games are left out.

commitResults.messageTitle: Record who lent or gave a game, and when it is due back
commitResults.messageBody: Adds borrow INDEX /from NAME [/due YYYY-MM-DD] and giveback INDEX (#54). list shows who each game is from and ends with a reminder of overdue games. Saved as the named fields from=NAME and due=DATE. Uses borrow instead of 'lend /from' from the issue, since lend already means lending a game out (#50). Borrowed games stay available to filter and pick, since they are on the user's shelf.

commitResults.messageTitle: Address review on #61: missing-prefix hint, aligned help, logging
commitResults.messageBody: unavailable 2 missing now asks 'Did you forget /reason?' instead of reporting '2 missing' as a bad INDEX. Help rows are padded to one width so unavailable lines up with the rest, and the UG's help output is copied from the code again (it was missing rate/unrate). UnavailableCommand and AvailableCommand log the change at FINE, like edit and rate.

commitResults.messageTitle: Address review on #62: giveback removes loans, refuses gifts
commitResults.messageBody: giveback now removes a borrowed game from the collection, since it is no longer on the shelf and filter and pick should stop suggesting it, and refuses gifts (no due date), which have nothing to give back. borrow compares the old and new record before changing the game, so the 'already recorded' error never modifies it. Also adds a 'Did you forget /from?' hint and FINE logging to borrow and giveback, matching the fixes to unavailable in #61.
